No arithmetic is shown.","reason":"The first visibly omits a multiplicity factor; the second supplies an incorrect number without calculations establishing its cause.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J02856","case1_error":"Counts Reece's ladder only once, omitting his 15 climbs.","case2_error":"Subtracts signed velocities instead of speed magnitudes, obtaining 800 rather than 40 feet per second.","reason":"Omitting repeated climbs differs from confusing velocity with speed.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J02857","case1_error":"Treats the car payment as 20% of gross income instead of after-tax income.","case2_error":"Adds tax to gross pay instead of subtracting it to obtain take-home pay.","reason":"The first assigns a percentage to the wrong income base; the second reverses the effect of a tax deduction.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J02858","case1_error":"Assigns two legs to each of the other walker's dogs, then rounds the resulting invalid fractional dog count.","case2_error":"Uses P = 2L; whether 'other citations' means each other category or their combined total is materially ambiguous.","reason":"The first has a clear counting error. The second depends on an ambiguous comparison scope, so a shared error mechanism cannot be established.","judgment":"uncertain"},{"pair_id":"J02859","case1_error":"Uses the final tank count as the original count when calculating how many fish were caught.","case2_error":"Subtracts losses from an already-final score; additionally, points per win do not determine total rounds played.","reason":"The second contains erroneous score accounting, but the requested total rounds is underdetermined without information about losing rounds, making the case materially ambiguous.","judgment":"uncertain"}]}
